h: Edwardian Elegance and More Leeds Days Out
p: Lotherton Hall was home to the Gascoigne family, who gave the house and its estate to the city of Leeds in the 1960s. Inside you'll find period rooms, collections of art and fashion, and plenty of stories about the family who lived there. It's a great add-on if you've got an older child who likes a bit of history, or grandparents who'd enjoy a sit-down among the antiques after a wander round the birds.

To make the day go smoothly, start with the wildlife while energy levels are high, then move onto the gardens and the hall. Picnic tables and grassy areas make it easy to eat outdoors, so packing lunch is a good shout. Wear sensible shoes, because the estate paths and grass can get soggy, and give yourselves a good few hours.

Leeds has a wonderful spread of family days out to tie in with a visit. Temple Newsam, on the eastern side of the city, is a grand Tudor-Jacobean house with a working rare-breeds farm and huge parkland to explore. Roundhay Park, in the north of the city, has lakes, woodland and Tropical World, a warm indoor attraction with butterflies and animals from hotter climates. In the city centre, the Royal Armouries Museum on the waterfront houses an incredible collection of arms and armour, and it's free to enter. Kirkgate Market is a cracking place to grab a bite and soak up the atmosphere, especially on a busy Saturday. All that within easy reach makes Leeds a top pick for a family weekend.
